(1) No person maintaining, servicing, repairing, or 
            
            disposing of an appliance or industrial process refrigeration may knowingly vent or otherwise release into the environment any refrigerant from such appliances. Notwithstanding any other provision of this subpart, the following substitutes in the following end-uses are exempt from this prohibition and from the requirements of this subpart:

(2) 
            De minimis
             releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerants are not subject to this prohibition. Except for exempt substitutes, refrigerant releases are 
            de minimis
             only if they occur when:

(i) The applicable practices in §§ 82.155 and 82.156 are observed, the applicable practices in § 82.157 are observed for appliances that contain any class I or class II refrigerant or blend containing a class I or class II refrigerant, recovery and/or recycling machines that meet the requirements in § 82.158 are used whenever refrigerant is removed from an appliance, the technician certification provisions in § 82.161 are observed, and the reclamation requirements in § 82.164 are observed; or

(ii) The requirements in subpart B of this part are observed.

judgments.label: negative
judgments.rationale: Paragraph (a)(3) (C0003) makes knowing release of refrigerant after recovery an outright violation. Paragraph (a)(2) applies only to releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover, not intentional venting of refrigerant after recovery. Treating C0002 as qualifying C0003 would wrongly allow intentional release of recovered refrigerant under the guise of de minimis.

judgments.label: positive
judgments.rationale: The proposed change adds qualifications linking the stopping exemption in paragraph (b)(1) to both C0000 (the stopping, listening, and looking requirement) and C0002 (the prohibition against shifting gears while crossing tracks). Under 49 CFR 392.10(b), the exemption is explicitly limited to stopping ('A stop need not be made at...'). It does not qualify or excuse the driver from the prohibition against shifting gears while crossing the tracks set forth in C0002.

source_spans.quote: (a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, the driver of a commercial motor vehicle specified in paragraphs (a) (1) through (6) of this section shall not cross a railroad track or tracks at grade unless he/she first: Stops the commercial motor vehicle within 50 feet of, and not closer than 15 feet to, the tracks; thereafter listens and looks in each direction along the tracks for an approaching train; and ascertains that no train is approaching. When it is safe to do so, the driver may drive the commercial motor vehicle across the tracks in a gear that permits the commercial motor vehicle to complete the crossing without a change of gears. The driver must not shift gears while crossing the tracks.

(b) A stop need not be made at:

(1) A streetcar crossing, or railroad tracks used exclusively for industrial switching purposes, within a business district, as defined in § 390.5 of this chapter.

judgments.label: positive
judgments.rationale: Passage F013 establishes that de minimis releases are 'not subject to this prohibition', which solely targets the venting prohibition under paragraph (a)(1) (C0000). The text does not make de minimis releases an exemption to the separate violation rule for knowing release after recovery in paragraph (a)(3) (C0003), nor does it exempt parties from the affirmative practice and equipment requirements of paragraph (b) (C0004). In fact, observing those practices and using certified equipment is an express prerequisite under paragraph (a)(2)(i) for a release to qualify as de minimis. Qualifying C0003 and C0004 is therefore unsupported.

judgments.rationale: Paragraph (a) opens with an express caveat ('Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section') to the general prohibition against crossing without first stopping, listening, and looking. Paragraph (b)(1) specifies that a stop need not be made at streetcar crossings or industrial switching tracks in a business district, directly excepting those crossings from C0000.
